title: Skybeam Networks - Perf mode selection & p95 probe
summary: Intro + qualification on user patterns (short chat replies + long summaries), target p95 numbers discussed, rough token/sec and concurrency modelling, preferred hosting (VPC+Dedic), questions on SOC2/KMS and audit logs. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: streaming tokenbench + p95 probe on a 10k qps simulated workload, SE to share benchmark harness and pricing ballpark.
next_steps: Redwood to share perf kit (streaming tokenbench script) and SOC2 docs - Priya to send by 2028-03-11
Schedule pilot kickoff (2-week) - Ethan to propose slots by 2028-03-12
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and 3 canonical prompt sets - Laila to send by 2028-03-13
action_items: Priya Nair: send perf kit + security packet (SOC2, ISO) - due 2028-03-11
Ethan Rogers: send pricing/hosted vs dedicated comparison and pilot contract draft - due 2028-03-12
Laila Ortiz: upload sample prompts + token distribution + expected p95 SLOs - due 2028-03-13
transcript:
Date: 2028-03-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Rogers, Priya Nair, Liam Beck (Redwood); Oliver Chen, Laila Ortiz, Marcus Wu, Nina Patel (Skybeam)

Summary: quick qualification then dive into p95 and token/sec targets. Lots of back-and-forth about streaming latencies and reserved capacity. Some transcription noise.

00:00 Ethan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick intros - i'm ethan, AE on the redwood team, priya's our SE who will run the perf bits, liam helps on solutions.
00:14 Oliver: hey, oliver here, ct o at skybeam, we do edge routing and realtime chat assistance for ISPs, latency is like a life or death thing for us so want to understand p95 really well.
00:28 Laila: hi, laila, lead ml, we own pipeline and model selection - our main flows are short assistant replies ~20-60 tokens and long summary jobs ~500-1k tokens, streaming matters a lot.
00:45 Priya: awesome, can you share your target p95 numbers? is it per-token stream p95 or end-to-end response?
00:58 Laila: for short replies we need end-to-end p95 < 200ms ideally, for streaming where token arrives progressively maybe p95 token latency < 80ms would be great, and for summary jobs p95 can be higher like < 2s but throughput matters.
01:20 Liam: quick note re hosting modes — hosted api will be easiest for fast time-to-value, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and more predictable p95 at scale, private (vpc/on prem) is for compliance. any preference?
01:40 Marcus: security wise, we need VPC peering and KMS integration, plus SOC2 cert is mandatory for procurement. Also, we do want audit logs retained for 12 months.
01:55 Priya: we support VPC and KMS, and we can expose audit logs; i will attach the SOC2 report.
02:05 Oliver: cool. question on cost - if we insist on p95 < 200ms for short replies, what's the unit cost impact vs relaxing to 300ms?
02:18 Priya: high level, latency SLOs drive instance sizing and reserved capacity. shaving from 300ms to 200ms often requires higher dedicated pool or higher priority routing which increases unit cost ~20-40% depending on concurrency and model. but caching and prefix caching can help a lot for repeated prompts.
02:35 Ethan: also tradeoffs with batching - if you batch aggressively you save tokens/cost but increase tail latency; continuous batching and smart routing let you get some wins without crushing p95.
02:50 Nina: timeline - procurement wants vendor decision in 6 weeks, pilot this month if possible.
03:03 Ethan: ok noted. priya — can we sketch a pilot that proves p95 and token/sec?
03:12 Priya: yes — suggest a 2-week pilot: first week smoke runs for correctness and connectivity, second week full tokenbench with streaming enabled. we'll run two scenarios: short chat (20-60 tokens) at concurrency 800-1200 rps and long summary at concurrency 60-100 with sustained token/sec.
03:33 Laila: those concurrencies feel right-ish; our peak qps is 1.1k for short chats, average 300. bursts to 2k for promotions.
03:45 Priya: for the streaming test we measure: per-token p95 (ms), server-side token/sec (tokens/sec per GPU), observed end-to-end p95 (first token and last token), and cold start tail. we'll also measure kv cache hit rate if you enable prefix caching.
04:03 Marcus: what's expected tokens/sec per GPU for the models we use? we run an open Llama variant around the 70B family (quantized).
04:18 Priya: with 70B quantized on A100-style equivalent we typically see ~600-1200 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and attention optimizations; nv kernel selection can push those numbers; smaller models or higher quantization get higher tokens/sec. exact numbers vary, we'll run the benchmark on your prompt sets.
04:40 Oliver: do you have any internal fallback options if capacity gets saturated during bursts?
04:48 Priya: yes — smart routing can fall back to a compatible smaller model or route to another region or dedicated burst pool. we can set automated fallback policies to maintain latency SLOs at some quality tradeoff.
05:02 Laila: how about multiplexing client-side? we already pipeline 4 requests per connection - will that interfere?
05:12 Priya: that helps, but we also need server-side continuous batching to be tuned so p95 doesn't spike. we can share recommended client concurrency and backpressure heuristics in the perf kit.
05:30 Ethan: any regulatory constraints we should know?
05:36 Marcus: data residency — some EU traffic must stay in eu-west region; also enterprise customers will require SAML SSO and RBAC.
05:46 Priya: redwood supports region pinning for routing, SAML SSO, and role-based access. we'll include deployment topology options (hosted with region controls, dedicated in a managed vpc, or private with your k8s).
06:02 Oliver: what about cold starts? our users hate a single first-token spike.
06:09 Priya: we have warm pool and pre-warming strategies; with dedicated capacity you can keep a warm pool which reduces cold-start p95 dramatically. for hosted we offer burst warmers and keepalive options too.
06:24 Laila: can you explain the p95 measurement — how do you measure streaming token p95 vs end-to-end p95?
06:32 Priya: streaming token p95 is measured per token latency (time from server generation to client receipt) sampling tokens across sequences. end-to-end p95 is request-to-last-byte. we report both and break down by token position.
06:48 Oliver: do you instrument tracing with token-level timestamps? we use those for SLO alerts.
06:55 Priya: yes we can dump a trace with per-token timestamps and include it in the console.
07:05 Marcus: procurement will ask about pricing model — do you bill per token for streaming as usual? what about reserved capacity pricing?
07:15 Ethan: hosted is per-token; dedicated has a base monthly reserved fee plus a token usage component; private is license/ops fee. we'll give a ballpark in the pricing doc.
07:26 Nina: any limits on concurrency per connection? our gateway maintains many long-lived streams.
07:33 Priya: we support multiplexed streams; limits depend on backend instance sizing. in dedicated you can control max concurrent streams per node. we'll provide recommended maxs in perf notes.
07:45 Laila: question on KV cache - will it help with our repeated prefix in sessions?
07:52 Priya: yes — kv cache / prefix cache helps reduce repeated compute for common history. we also support partial cache invalidation and targeted cache retention policies.
08:03 Oliver: what's your experience hitting p95 < 200ms for short chat with 1k concurrent? any customers?
08:12 Priya: yes — our finance chat partners run ~800-1k rps with optimized models and dedicated pools hitting ~180-220ms p95 for short replies; that took structured batching, prefix caching and tuned kernels. we can show a case study.
08:28 Ethan: i'll attach that case study and a short benchmark sheet.
08:33 Laila: can the pilot run on our VPC or do you need to bring traffic to your hosted endpoint?
08:40 Priya: we can do either — recommended for security is dedicated in your VPC or private deployment, but for initial benchmarks hosted with a peered VPC is fastest to start.
08:54 Marcus: latency added by network egress to hosted could be substantial from our EU edge — want to see numbers.
09:01 Priya: we'll include region-specific network latency in the pilot and recommend edge routing or regional dedicated pools.
09:12 Laila: what's the benchmark harness look like? do you accept our load generator?
09:18 Priya: yes — we can run our harness and also accept your k6/locust profile. we'll need sample prompts and the client concurrency parameters.
09:30 Oliver: sample prompts we'll provide. what about data retention and logs during pilot? we need to ensure no PII leaves our control.
09:38 Priya: pilot can be done in VPC peered mode with redwood not persisting logs by default, we can set retention to zero for pilot traces. i'll confirm in writing.
09:50 Ethan: ok, let's map success criteria — what should success look like for you?
09:58 Laila: pass criteria: short chat p95 <= 220ms 95% of test windows during peak sim, streaming token p95 <= 100ms, long summary throughput >= X tokens/sec for N workers — we'll define exact numbers in the profile.
10:16 Priya: sounds good; we'll include measurement windows and how we sample p95.
10:22 Oliver: procurement: we need SOC2 report, contract terms, and a simple SLA for pilot.
10:30 Ethan: we'll send SOC2 and a short pilot MSA; pricing will be ballpark until we have benchmark results.
10:38 Nina: any blockers on your side to start pilot this week?
10:44 Priya: no blockers — i need sample prompts and network egress tests. we'll propose kickoff tomorrow if you can provide that.
10:55 Laila: we can aim for tomorrow for kickoff if you can send the perf kit now.
11:03 Priya: i'll do that tonight.
11:07 Ethan: ok great. quick deep dive — Priya, maybe show a couple of numbers about tokens/sec for quantized 70B?
11:14 Priya: sure — rough: 70B quantized on specialized infra: 700-1000 tokens/sec sustained on a single GPU for medium sequences (256); for longer sequences tokens/sec drops, and attention patterns matter. with optimized kernels and sequence bucketing we can improve effective throughput by ~20%.
11:37 Marcus: how does model version pinning work if we do dedicated? we need stable behavior for legal/regulatory reasons.
11:45 Priya: model pinning is supported — you can pin exact model hash and control rollouts via canary or A/B policies. all inference versions produce audit logs.
11:56 Laila: any limitations with function calling/structured output streaming? we rely on function calling heavily.
12:03 Priya: function calling is supported in streaming; we can stream JSON chunks and provide schema validation hooks. we'll test that in the pilot.
12:17 Oliver: ok let's recap next steps.
12:22 Ethan: recap: priya sends perf kit + SOC2 + case study tonight, ethan sends pricing and pilot contract draft by sunday, customer sends prompts and traffic profile by monday. schedule pilot kickoff for monday afternoon.
12:38 Nina: sounds good.
12:44 Laila: small note — we'd like a dedicated contact for the pilot, can that be priya?
12:49 Priya: yes, i'll be primary SE contact.
12:53 Oliver: thanks everyone, bye.
12:55 Ethan: thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear: "dedicated" transcribed as "deducted" in one snippet, some product names may be off.

Attachments referenced: "perf_kit_v1.zip" (sent after call), "soc2_summary.pdf" (to be sent), "case_study_finance_chat.xlsx" (benchmark sheet)

End of transcript.
